question.problem: The graph of the function $y=f(x)$ passes through $(4,5)$ and is concave up on the interval $(2,5).$ If ${f}^{′}(4)=-2,$ estimate the value of $f(4.4)$ using the tangent line approximation of $f(x)$ at $x=4$ and determine whether the approximation is an underestimate or overestimate.
question.worked_solution:
The tangent line approximation of $f(x)$ at the point $a=4$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}L(x) & =f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a) \\  & =f(4)+{f}^{′}(4)(x-4).\end{aligned}
$$

The graph of the function passes through the point $(4,5),$ so we have $f(4)=5.$ Also, we're told that ${f}^{′}(4)=-2,$ so we get

$$
\begin{aligned}L(x) & =5+(-2)(x-4) \\  & =5-2x+8 \\  & =-2x+13.\end{aligned}
$$

We can approximate $f(4.4)$ by evaluating the tangent line approximation at $x=4.4.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(4.4) & ≈L(4.4) \\  & =-2(4.4)+13 \\  & =-8.8+13 \\  & =4.2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the function is concave up on the interval $(2,5),$ the linear approximation $L(x)$ is below the graph near $x=4,$ and therefore we have an underestimate.
